title: ACM, TLS & Encryption in Transit
summary: Public and private certificates, TLS termination points and end-to-end encryption choices.
tldr: **ACM** issues free public TLS certificates for integrated services (ALB, NLB, CloudFront, API Gateway) and **renews them automatically** when they are DNS-validated and in use.
Internal hostnames such as `*.corp.internal` can't get public certificates. Use **AWS Private CA** and request private certificates through ACM.
To *force* encryption in transit, enforce it at the resource: an S3 bucket policy on `aws:SecureTransport`, `require_secure_transport` on RDS MySQL, or an HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect on the ALB.

keyFacts.text: A certificate used by **CloudFront** must be requested or imported in US East (N. Virginia). ALB and NLB certificates live in the load balancer's own Region.
Keeping the validation CNAME record in DNS (for example Route 53) lets ACM renew managed certificates with **no human step**. Email validation needs someone to approve.
ACM **never** renews certificates you import from a third-party CA. You must reimport them yourself before they expire.
The TLS versions and ciphers an ALB or NLB accepts are set by the **listener security policy**, not by the certificate.
**CloudFront field-level encryption** encrypts chosen form fields at the edge with a public key, so only the service with the private key can read them.

keywords.cue: certificates expired, renew automatically with no manual steps
keywords.answer: ACM public certificate with DNS validation

keywords.cue: TLS certificate for a CloudFront distribution
private domain such as corp.internal, trusted by internal clients
keywords.answer: AWS Private CA with private certificates issued through ACM

keywords.cue: reject any S3 request over plain HTTP
keywords.answer: Bucket policy Deny when aws:SecureTransport is false
require_secure_transport (MySQL) or rds.force_ssl (PostgreSQL) in a parameter group

keywords.cue: require TLS 1.2 or later on the ALB
keywords.answer: HTTPS listener with a TLS 1.2/1.3 security policy

keywords.cue: users typing http:// must be sent to HTTPS
keywords.answer: ALB HTTP listener redirect action to port 443

keywords.cue: only one microservice may ever see a sensitive form field
offload TLS from the web servers
keywords.answer: Terminate TLS on the ALB or CloudFront with an ACM certificate

traps: A CloudWatch alarm or Config rule on certificate expiry only **warns** you. It doesn't renew anything.
You can't get an ACM **public** certificate for a private, non-routable domain name.
Encryption at rest (SSE-KMS, RDS storage encryption) does nothing for data **in transit**.
End-to-end HTTPS still decrypts at every hop. If intermediate services must not see a field, use field-level encryption.
Removing port 80 from a security group doesn't redirect users. Browsers just fail to connect.
